First-Time Setup

The exact order of commands to go from a fresh clone to a running API backed by a real, seeded database.

Every piece needed to run this project locally has now been introduced separately — this topic is just the checklist that ties them together, in the order they actually need to run. Starting from a fresh clone (or after deleting your local database entirely):

docker compose up -d mysql
npx prisma migrate dev --name init
npx prisma db seed
npm run dev
  1. Start MySQL (containerized MySQL topic) — -d runs it in the background. Give it a few seconds to finish starting before the next step; prisma migrate dev will simply fail to connect and tell you to retry if you're too quick.
  2. Apply migrations (migrations topic) — creates every table from schema.prisma in the now-empty database. Only the very first migration needs an explicit --name; npm run db:migrate (Figure 2.3) is the equivalent shortcut for ones after this.
  3. Seed it (seeding topic) — populates realistic dev data across every table. npm run db:seed is the shortcut for the same command.
  4. Start the app — exactly the npm run dev from Lesson 1; nothing about running the app changed, only what ticket.service.js does once a request reaches it (coming up two topics from now).

Skipping straight to step 4 without the first three still starts the server fine — Express doesn't know or care whether a database exists yet — but the first request that actually queries MySQL fails, since there's nothing there to query.
